newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos accepts Manila defence chief's resignation.
newsitem.headline: Ramos accepts Manila defence chief's resignation.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Wednesday he had accepted the resignation of Defence chief Renato de Villa who last month launched a bid to run for the country's top post next year.

"Even as I approve your resignation effective September 15, I commend you for your exemplary stewardship of the Department of National Defence," Ramos said in a letter to de Villa, a copy of which was released to reporters.
De Villa resigned after announcing his candidacy for president on July 20.
Ramos has yet to choose a replacement for de Villa.
De Villa, 62, a former army general who has fared badly in popularity polls, joins a dozen others, including a former movie star, in the contest to succeed Ramos.
Besides de Villa, seven other members of the ruling Lakas party have signalled their intention to run.
They will fight for the party's nomination in November or December. The presidential elections will be held in May 1998.
Ramos, whose six-year term ends in June next year, is constitutionally barred from running for a second term.
Widely regarded as the front-runner of the race is Vice-President Joseph "Erap" Estrada, who counts on his huge appeal as a former action star in local movies.
The others include opposition senator Gloria Macapagal Arroyo, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo, Ramos' sister, senator Leticia Ramos Shahani, and Lower House Speaker Jose de Venecia.
